prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 1997 Scottish manifesto (policy-focused, non-ideological)

- Route to independence: Seek a majority of Scottish MPs, open negotiations with the UK and EU, then hold a single-question referendum on the settlement within 6–12 months. On approval, declare independence and hold fresh national elections.

- Constitutional design: Introduce a written constitution and Bill of Rights guaranteeing civil, social, and workplace rights (including a minimum wage). Create a single-chamber parliament elected by proportional representation, extend voting to 16+, allow public petitions, and entrench local government (also elected by PR). Reform the monarchy’s role and finance; Chancellor of the Parliament to sign laws.

- Economic strategy and taxation: Target full employment, forecasting 100,000 additional jobs and a national apprenticeship scheme. Cut corporation tax (main rate to 30p; small companies to 18p), abolish Class IV National Insurance for the self‑employed, cap business rate increases to inflation, and introduce banded business rates aiding smaller firms. Establish export and skills bodies, boost R&D (+£120m over four years), and double tourism marketing. Personal tax: introduce a 15p starter rate, widen the basic-rate band by 15%, remove the National Insurance ceiling, and cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5% (seek scope for further reduction).

- Debt and fiscal stance: Inherit a population share of UK debt (~£38bn) and repay £6.6bn over four years. Publish a fully costed four-year budget showing net resources for spending, investment, and debt reduction.

- Health and social care: Replace the internal market with an integrated, nationally planned and locally delivered system; create national and local Health Commissions; add £35m per year and cut administration. Reinstate NHS dentistry, review prescription charges, ban tobacco advertising, raise tobacco duty, and strengthen nutrition and food safety via an independent Food and Consumer Health Agency. Abolish means-testing for residential elderly care.

- Social policy: Raise Child Benefit to £12.50 per week, restore benefits for 16–17-year-olds, increase state pensions (£3 single; £5 couple per week), introduce a Cold Climate Allowance, and remove standing charges for pensioners’ utilities.

- Justice and safety: Support community-focused “zero tolerance” policing, strengthen Procurator Fiscal resources, expand alternatives to prison with evidence-based rehabilitation, intensify anti-drugs measures, and ban handguns with a national firearms register.

- Education and training: Hire 700 teachers, upgrade school buildings, provide internet access in every school and computers in every classroom, offer free nursery education for all 3–4-year-olds, restore student maintenance grants (1990 real level), and expand youth/adult training (+£50m per year). Support Gaelic medium education and wider cultural/faith provision.

- Housing and local services: Transfer 75% of council housing debt to central government within four years (rest thereafter), enabling up to 20,000 new social homes, 35,000 homes restored above tolerable standard, and 160,000 treated for damp/condensation. Protect new/improved stock from discounted right-to-buy. Replace Scottish Homes with an accountable housing agency. Abolish water quangos and return services to democratic control.

- Land, rural economy, and sectors: Abolish feudal tenure; create a Scottish Land Commission and an open land register; transfer Crown coastal/seabed powers to local councils. Reform crofting (new development agency). Agriculture: rapid beef traceability, CAP reform toward active land workers, diversification fund (£10m/year). Fisheries: regional management, stronger enforcement, processing support, marketing, harbour upgrades (+£10m/year). Forestry: replace the Forestry Commission with a National Forest Enterprise Board; double woodland cover in 25 years, prioritising native species.

- Environment and energy: Strengthen SEPA’s independence and remit; set national environmental targets; end nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay and pivot to cleanup, storage, decommissioning, and a renewables R&D centre. Plan a phased nuclear power exit while expanding renewables and conservation. Support long-term North Sea activity under existing legal sector boundaries; address gas transmission pricing; encourage petrochemicals.

- Transport and telecoms: Return Scottish Railtrack assets to public ownership; modernise/electrify key lines; integrate bus/coach with rail. Replace Skye Bridge tolls with shadow tolls and bring into public ownership; move toward removing bridge tolls. Strengthen lifeline ferries, adjust Air Passenger Duty for remote areas, and expand international links. Enhance rural telecoms, support distance learning, promote teleworking, expand internet access in schools and business, and update laws on cyber abuse without adding new censorship.

- External relations and defence: Full EU membership with representation in institutions, focus on fisheries and agricultural reforms, and maximise EU funding. Maintain targeted diplomatic posts and join the Commonwealth, Council of Europe, UN, and a proposed British Isles association. Create Scottish Defence Forces (specified Army, Navy, Air Force strengths), prioritise joint training and peacekeeping (with a new college), remove nuclear weapons from the Clyde, phase out NATO membership due to nuclear policy while maintaining cooperation through European and partnership frameworks, and promote defence diversification.

- International aid: Increase official development assistance toward 0.7% of GDP within six years.
